question: Which of the following is a mechanism of progression of chronic kidney disease regardless of its etiology?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Hyperfiltration" -> "increased glomerular pressure" -> "glomerular damage" -> "progression of chronic kidney disease" -> 80% CHAIN: "Malnutrition" -> "reduced renal function" -> "progression of chronic kidney disease" -> 70% CHAIN: "Hyperkalemia" -> "disruption of renal function" -> "progression of chronic kidney disease" -> 75% CHAIN: "Acidosis" -> "interstitial fibrosis" -> "progression of chronic kidney disease" -> 80%
enhanced_information: Hyperfiltration leading to increased glomerular pressure and subsequent glomerular damage is a mechanism of progression of chronic kidney disease regardless of its etiology. Malnutrition, hyperkalemia, and acidosis can also contribute to the progression of chronic kidney disease through various pathways.
analysis: Hyperfiltration leading to increased glomerular pressure and subsequent glomerular damage is a well-established mechanism of progression of chronic kidney disease regardless of its etiology. While malnutrition, hyperkalemia, and acidosis can also contribute to the progression of chronic kidney disease, hyperfiltration is a primary mechanism that directly impacts the kidneys.
